review_scope: Bounded source and assertion review at b901326c. Neither whole-clause nor whole-ADR certification. Draft/run statements describe reviewer handoff; current execution and parent qualifications are in findings.json and gate-results.json.

reviewer_record.feature: Structure root discovery and ordered hierarchy
reviewer_record.title: The structure tree root is located from Catalog /StructTreeRoot; root /K children define order and are structure elements.
reviewer_record.source: Effective ISO 32000-2 p.722, §14.7.2 and Table 354; Tables 354–355. Producer-side type requirements are not reader rejection mandates.
reviewer_record.errata: None directly affecting hierarchy. Table heading in EC3 source checked against PDF footer.
reviewer_record.ledger: §14.7.2 implemented; crates/pdf-model/src/structure.rs, structure/logical.rs, structure/owners.rs; tests include tree/role and cycle.
reviewer_record.assertions: Existing exact-offset PDF builders assert successful open but the structure unit helper does not explicitly assert !was_recovered; largest-tree integration exercises real corpus. Order test confirms depth-first parent-first /K order.
reviewer_record.verdict: supported with a resource-limit reporting defect
residuals: children() and identified_children() silently take only MAX_CHILDREN=65,536; descend() silently returns at MAX_DEPTH=64. Neither marks Walk.truncated, whose current flag only represents MAX_ELEMENTS. A valid larger fan-out/depth can therefore be exposed as a complete prefix.
Draft hierarchy_truncation_draft.rs adds exact-xref no-recovery, small positive control, and assertions accepting either full traversal or an explicitly reported bound.

reviewer_record.title: The name tree maps unique element ID byte strings to structure elements when IDs are present.
reviewer_record.source: Effective ISO 32000-2 p.722, Table 354 and Table 355; §7.9.6 governs name-tree structure.
reviewer_record.errata: None directly affecting this feature.
reviewer_record.ledger: §14.7.2 implemented; structure/owners.rs element_by_id and pdf-transform structure reconciliation/writing.
tests: crates/pdf-transform/tests/merge.rs tests for IDTree collisions and preservation
reviewer_record.assertions: Synthetic unique-ID tree resolves requested element; merge fixture covers collisions and output tree. Unit fixture uses generated offsets, though its helper does not explicitly assert !was_recovered.
reviewer_record.verdict: supported for lookup and transformation paths sampled
residuals: No current assertion in the reviewed unit locates duplicate IDs as a reader error; uniqueness is a producer rule. Reader behavior should remain permissive unless a separate diagnostic is intended.

reviewer_record.title: ParentTree is a number tree mapping page/content stream or object keys to parents; next key is greater than used keys and used by writers.
reviewer_record.source: Effective ISO 32000-2 pp.749–750; Table 354 /ParentTree; parent tree narrative and Table 359.
reviewer_record.errata: EC3 #452 renumbers old §14.7.5.4 to effective §14.7.5.5; #343 changes a quantifier in parent-tree narrative without changing the lookup mechanism; #463 clarifies the exact StructParent/StructParents pair.
reviewer_record.ledger: §14.7.2, §14.7.5.4 (2020 heading; effective .5) implemented; ParentTree model and pdf-transform writer/reconciliation.
reviewer_record.assertions: Tests cover number-tree key lookup, zero-based array indexing, one-reference object form, page/annotation/form keys and writer carry/update. Core test helper generates xref offsets but does not assert no recovery.
reviewer_record.verdict: supported with effective-number ledger drift
residuals: Ledger still names the post-renumber sequence by 2020 headings (§14.7.5.4 for ParentTree); effective citations shift to §14.7.5.5.
Malformed absent keys are returned as empty/None; this is permissive reader behavior, not proof of a reader error obligation.

reviewer_record.title: Root role and class maps are consumed by the corresponding structure type and attribute readers.
reviewer_record.source: Effective ISO 32000-2 pp.722, 727 and 753; Table 354 /RoleMap and /ClassMap.
reviewer_record.errata: EC3 #289 adds ordering when multiple class objects define the same attribute; effective number for attribute classes is unchanged.
reviewer_record.ledger: §14.7.2, §14.7.3, §14.7.6.2 implemented; role mapping and attribute readers split across structure/roles.rs and structure/attributes.rs.
reviewer_record.assertions: Transitive role mapping and class map order tests give distinct expected standard type and attribute values.
reviewer_record.verdict: supported for tested map forms
residuals: The names and values are interpreted by separate downstream clauses; this feature row does not certify every role vocabulary or every class-owner attribute.

reviewer_record.feature: Root namespaces list and element namespace membership
reviewer_record.title: A tagged document's explicit namespaces are declared at the root and an element's own /NS selects its role map.
reviewer_record.source: Effective ISO 32000-2 pp.722, 739–741; Table 354 /Namespaces; §14.8.6.2 explicit namespace rule.
reviewer_record.errata: EC3 #396 adds root listing to the relevant requirement language; EC3 #93 marks Table 355 /R deprecated in PDF 2.0, not a namespace change.
reviewer_record.ledger: §14.7.2 and §14.7.4 implemented; 2020 ledger note states writer completeness for root Namespaces and role walk reads each element /NS.
reviewer_record.assertions: Tests give root RoleMap and element NS RoleMapNS disagreeing targets, and transitive target namespace. Conformance diagnostics count explicitly declared foreign namespaces; processor does not reject malformed documents.
reviewer_record.verdict: supported for namespace selection; producer listing requirement is not reader rejection
residuals: The root array's membership requirement is producer conformance; no claim that reader must reject an element whose NS dictionary is not listed. Tests do not exhaust namespace listing mutations.

reviewer_record.feature: Structure type and root role map traversal
reviewer_record.title: Structure element /S is a name; RoleMap associations are applied transitively, including standard-name keys, and circular chains terminate.
reviewer_record.source: Effective ISO 32000-2 p.727, §14.7.3, including NOTE 2.
reviewer_record.errata: None directly affecting role map text.
reviewer_record.ledger: §14.7.3 implemented; structure/roles.rs, standard type mapping.
reviewer_record.assertions: Transitive custom-to-custom-to-standard path; cycle with a known type; cycle without standard; name/namespace controls.
reviewer_record.verdict: supported with an explicit cycle interpretation
residuals: ADR 2028 chooses the first standard type along a cycle; this is a reading of NOTE 2's stop condition and has dedicated fixture evidence, not an unambiguous rule that every circular map yields one canonical role.

reviewer_record.title: Namespace-specific map values may be a default-namespace name or [target name, target namespace reference]; mappings may be transitive.
reviewer_record.source: Effective ISO 32000-2 pp.740–741; Table 356 and NOTE 3.
reviewer_record.errata: None directly affecting Table 356.
reviewer_record.ledger: §14.7.4.2 implemented; Namespace and role walk in structure.rs and structure/roles.rs.
reviewer_record.assertions: Single-name map uses default standard namespace; array form routes to target namespace then standard role.
reviewer_record.verdict: supported for both declared forms
residuals: No tests cover malformed array arity/type or direct rather than indirect target references; these are producer-validity issues, not required reader rejection.

reviewer_record.title: Namespace name is a text string used for uniqueness, conventionally a URI that need not resolve; optional schema file spec has no required format.
reviewer_record.source: Effective ISO 32000-2 pp.740–741, Table 356 and NOTES 1–2.
reviewer_record.errata: None affecting Table 356.
reviewer_record.ledger: §14.7.4.2 implemented; structure.rs Namespace::read retains schema object.
reviewer_record.assertions: Name comparisons use full decoded namespace string; no network resolution is attempted; schema remains raw object.
reviewer_record.verdict: supported for stated identity rule
residuals: The assigned test family does not assert preservation of arbitrary Schema file-spec shapes; fetching/processing schema is not required by this clause.

reviewer_record.title: When owner comes from NS, namespace name identifies it; names corresponding to Table 376 owner values are equivalent.
reviewer_record.source: Effective ISO 32000-2 p.741; closing paragraph after Table 356.
reviewer_record.errata: EC3 #354 changes owner wording in §14.7.6.1 but not this equivalence.
reviewer_record.ledger: §14.7.4.2 and §14.7.6 implemented; AttributeObject::effective_owner.
reviewer_record.assertions: PDF-native namespace owner ranks; foreign namespace attribute object is named/refused; field owner controls priority.
reviewer_record.verdict: supported with intentionally bounded equivalence set
residuals: The clause names no expanded URI-to-owner mapping. Code equates a namespace whose text equals a Table 376 owner; whether external common namespace URIs correspond to table owner names is not enumerated by the source and should not be inferred.

reviewer_record.title: A structure element's /K may mix child elements, marked-content sequence references, and whole-object references; content items are leaves.
reviewer_record.source: Effective ISO 32000-2 p.728–729; old printed heading 14.7.5.1.1; text otherwise unchanged by EC3 #452.
reviewer_record.errata: EC3 #452 moves Content items to effective §14.7.5.2 and shifts all later §14.7.5 headings by one.
reviewer_record.ledger: 2020 rows §14.7.5.1.1 / .2 / .3 / .4 are all marked implemented; their current citations are stale after #452.
reviewer_record.assertions: Mixed child fixture has nested structure element plus integer, MCR, OBJR and verifies order and distinct Child variants.
reviewer_record.verdict: supported for tested forms; bounded hierarchy gap applies
residuals: No explicit negative/producer-conformance check for nested content items, and reader need not reject such input. The same fixture's helper calculates xrefs but doesn't assert was_recovered=false.

reviewer_record.title: BDC/EMC sequence has MCID unique within its content stream; page contents' stream array is treated as one stream; sequence must be on one page.
reviewer_record.source: Effective ISO 32000-2 pp.729–748; effective §14.7.5.3; §14.6 content-stream sequence rule.
reviewer_record.errata: EC3 #308 adds a note that MCIDs are scoped by content stream and start at zero; same MCID may reappear across pages or XObjects. EC3 #452 shifts heading .2 to .3.
reviewer_record.ledger: 2020 §14.7.5.2 marked-content row implemented; content.rs + structure::ParentTree and logical association.
reviewer_record.assertions: Tests distinguish stream identity and same MCID in independent streams; ParentTree lookup uses stream/page key and MCID index. Exact-xref builders in integration helpers; some unit fixtures omit explicit recovery assertion.
reviewer_record.verdict: supported for page, form and appearance-stream cases sampled
residuals: Not a validator for producer rules such as MCID starting at zero or uniqueness; source says writer shall. No need to invent reader rejection.

reviewer_record.title: MCR names MCID and may override inherited Pg; Stm identifies non-page content stream; StmOwn identifies object owning Stm.
reviewer_record.source: Effective ISO 32000-2 pp.730–748, Table 357; EC3 #431 revises /Pg's requirement phrasing.
reviewer_record.errata: EC3 #431 makes MCR Pg 'Sometimes required' and clarifies precedence/requiredness; EC3 #452 renumbers this clause.
reviewer_record.ledger: 2020 §14.7.5.2 implemented; Child::MarkedContent carries page/stream/owner references.
reviewer_record.assertions: Tests distinguish Pg inheritance, Stm stream identity, StmOwn annotation owner and the sequence's marks/rectangle/control.
reviewer_record.verdict: supported for route and tested owner linkage
residuals: EC3 #431 is writer-requiredness language; parsing missing Pg is a permissive path and no reader error should be inferred.

reviewer_record.clause: Effective §14.7.5.3, form XObject content paragraphs and EXAMPLES 4–5
reviewer_record.title: Form invocation may be included as a whole within a page marked-content item, or the form stream may contain its own items; multiple invocations require first method per invocation.
reviewer_record.source: Effective ISO 32000-2 pp.731–734, marked-content sequence discussion and examples; renumbered by EC3 #452.
reviewer_record.errata: EC3 #452 shifts this material to effective .3; no semantic text change.
reviewer_record.ledger: 2020 §14.7.5.2 ledger note explicitly records stream/mark alternatives; model content stream owner and viewer accessibility consume either.
tests: viewer-core/tests/headless.rs form-stream logical text and StmOwn tests
reviewer_record.assertions: Appearance/form stream sequence gets matching MCID and geometry on the owner; page sequence stays separate.
reviewer_record.verdict: supported for exercised form and appearance paths
residuals: I did not independently inspect every multiple-Do invocation permutation in this bounded review; the clause's first-method restriction is a producer rule and no reader refusal is implied.

reviewer_record.title: OBJR identifies an entire indirect object and optional page; object reference is distinct from marking only part of an object's stream.
reviewer_record.source: Effective ISO 32000-2 pp.748–749, Table 358 and NOTES 1–2.
reviewer_record.errata: EC3 #431 and #339 clarify Pg override and requiredness when no containing-element Pg; EC3 #452 shifts heading .3 to .4.
reviewer_record.ledger: 2020 §14.7.5.3 implemented; Child::Object carries object/page and page accessibility resolves annotation/XObject.
reviewer_record.assertions: One object and inherited/overridden page tested; annotation's position/control comes from Rect and widget data. NOTE 2 repeat rendering distinction documented.
reviewer_record.verdict: supported for object identity and annotation consumers sampled
residuals: XObject placement from arbitrary multiple Do invocations is not supplied by OBJR (NOTE 2); placement via content invocation was not fully audited here.

reviewer_record.title: Number-tree key maps object content to one parent ref or stream/page MCIDs to indexed array; object key and content-stream key forms are exclusive.
reviewer_record.source: Effective ISO 32000-2 pp.749–750; parent-tree paragraphs and Table 359.
reviewer_record.errata: EC3 #343 changes phrase 'at least one' to 'a'; #463 names StructParent / StructParents explicitly; #452 shifts old .4 to effective .5.
reviewer_record.ledger: 2020 §14.7.5.4 implemented; model for_page/element and inverse elements_on_page; transform writes keys.
reviewer_record.assertions: Both number tree and index lookup tested; array and direct object values in fixtures; annotation, form, image keys; saved merger rewrites parent tree.
reviewer_record.verdict: supported for normal values and write paths; incomplete-input policy is permissive
residuals: No reader validation that required ParentTree/StructParent(s) exist or are mutually exclusive; those are producer constraints. `ParentTree::for_page` maps missing data to empty rather than error, appropriately avoiding an invented rejection.

reviewer_record.feature: Structure element metadata that accessibility consumes
reviewer_record.title: Element identity, text replacement/alternate text and language are represented for consumers; pronunciation hints are optional processing.
reviewer_record.source: Effective ISO 32000-2 pp.723–727, Table 355; §14.9.6 says pronunciation hints need not be processed.
reviewer_record.errata: EC3 #93 marks element /R deprecated PDF 2.0; #452 shifts content clauses only.
reviewer_record.ledger: §14.7.2 implemented; text_entry helpers, accessibility consumer and pronunciation tests.
reviewer_record.assertions: Alternative/expanded text, ActualText, inherited language and element ID paths used; phoneme test asserts Alt and Lang rather than returning phoneme.
reviewer_record.verdict: supported for modeled accessibility fields; no phoneme processing is a permitted choice
residuals: No bounded review of every language inheritance interaction with marked-content escapes; that belongs to §14.9.2 and prior shard.

reviewer_record.title: Optional /Ref identifies related structure elements; optional /R states revision counter, default 0 and may increment after processor modifications.
reviewer_record.source: Effective ISO 32000-2 pp.723–727, Table 355 and §14.7.6.3.
reviewer_record.errata: EC3 #93 deprecates /R in PDF 2.0. No #452 effect on Table 355.
reviewer_record.ledger: Table355 entries appear under §14.7.2 implemented; row notes focus on ID, language/text, content. Current reviewed model has no explicit /Ref accessor and does not use element /R.
reviewer_record.code: No direct structure::Tree API for /Ref or element /R found in crates/pdf-model/src/structure*. Source search: only attributes revision pairs and ID access.
tests: No dedicated /Ref or structure-element /R assertion found in reviewed test files.
reviewer_record.assertions: No positive or negative assertion for relationship references or reading the element revision field found.
reviewer_record.verdict: bounded review leaves this optional metadata unconsumed; not classified as a required reader defect
residuals: §14.7.3/14.7.2 don't require a processor to act on /Ref; the 'may increment' instruction is optional producer behavior. A future accessibility/reference feature could justify accessors, but this review finds no conformance mandate to reject or render differently.

reviewer_record.title: Attribute object is a dictionary or stream with /O; /NS may identify namespace owner; all other keys except NS represent attributes.
reviewer_record.source: Effective ISO 32000-2 p.752, §14.7.6.1 and Table 360.
reviewer_record.errata: EC3 #354 changes 'conforming product that owns' to 'owner of' without semantic change.
reviewer_record.ledger: §14.7.6.1 implemented; AttributeObject::read retains raw dictionary.
reviewer_record.code: crates/pdf-model/src/structure.rs:2977,3015,3068,3140; pdf-syntax::Object::as_dict accepts both dictionaries and streams.
tests: Draft attribute_stream_draft.rs adds stream and dictionary controls.
reviewer_record.assertions: Existing tests exercise dictionary-valued /A and /ClassMap objects; code path appears to accept stream dictionaries via Object::as_dict. Draft uses exact xref and asserts both values independently.
reviewer_record.verdict: supported by code inspection; stream form lacks direct assertion
residuals: Draft stream-valued attribute test was not compiled or run.

reviewer_record.feature: Attribute class attachment and in-class precedence
reviewer_record.title: ClassMap resolves C names to attribute objects/arrays; later class/object values take precedence as EC3 inserts.
reviewer_record.errata: EC3 #289 inserts rule that later /C class object across arrays wins; #226 updates cross-reference to Table 376.
reviewer_record.ledger: §14.7.6.2 implemented; attribute attachment/ordering and winner semantics.
reviewer_record.assertions: One test controls class vs A and later A; second tests classes with single object and array and later class object. Assertions have distinct expected arrays.
reviewer_record.verdict: supported including EC3 #289
residuals: ClassMap malformed or missing targets are ignored as reader recovery, not a normative rejection test.

reviewer_record.title: Array entries may be paired with a following integer revision; absent revision defaults zero; revision numbers deprecated in PDF 2.0.
reviewer_record.errata: EC3 #305 marks revision numbers deprecated and removes 'typically' qualifier in class object-array wording; reading remains necessary to parse name/object pairs.
reviewer_record.ledger: §14.7.6.3 implemented; paired() and AttributeObject revision.
reviewer_record.assertions: Expected revision list [3,0,4] distinguishes pair, unpaired default and later pair across C/A.
reviewer_record.verdict: supported for pair parsing
residuals: No test covers negative/non-integer revision values; those are producer validity constraints and not reader error requirements.

reviewer_record.title: Owner-specific A value, five PDF-native owner A value, class value, inheritable parent value and attribute default have ordered priority.
reviewer_record.source: Effective ISO 32000-2 pp.755–758, §14.8.5.2–.4. This behavior is outside the 14.7.6 mechanism but is needed to assess what it consumes.
reviewer_record.errata: EC3 #226 corrects the §14.7.6.2 reference; no winner rule change.
reviewer_record.ledger: §14.7.6 / §14.8.5 implemented; feature mechanism and owner data are separate rows.
reviewer_record.assertions: Tests compare owner priority, standard-owner priority, class priority, parent inheritance and defaults for selected attributes.
reviewer_record.verdict: supported for tested attributes/owners; not whole §14.8.5 review
residuals: Per-attribute inheritability/default and each owner/type belong to §14.8.5 tables; not exhaustively checked here. Ledger status alone does not certify them.

reviewer_record.title: UserProperties owner stores /P array; each user property has name/value and optional formatted/hidden fields; other value types need not be displayed but are not errors.
reviewer_record.source: Effective ISO 32000-2 pp.754–755, §14.7.6.4 and Tables 361–362.
reviewer_record.errata: None identified for these entries.
reviewer_record.ledger: §14.7.6.4 implemented; AttributeObject::user_properties.
reviewer_record.assertions: Fixture covers plain, formatted-vs-value, hidden. Raw PDF V is preserved with F beside it.
reviewer_record.verdict: supported for tested properties
residuals: No direct assertion for non-string V; code preserves Object values, aligning with clause's instruction not to treat other types as errors. The full EXAMPLE's every property is not reproduced.
